open_items: ILO blanket-403 provider_down episode: eighth occurrence, cycle 382, resolved by cycle 383 (one cycle, as usual). Priors: 244, 251, 260, 264, 272, 281, 321, all but 321 resolved within a single cycle (321 took two cycles, gateway-data-only tail at 322). Closed.

ILO gateway_issue, both gateway metadata and gateway data HTTP 403 together, direct healthy: first occurrence of this exact combination, cycle 384, resolved by cycle 385. Distinct from the gateway-data-only flap (cycles 322, 370, metadata still passing) and from the gateway-metadata-500 episode (cycles 268-269, HTTP 500 not 403, data still passing). Occurred with a fully healthy cycle (383) in between it and the cycle 382 provider_down episode, so not a direct tail. Watch for a second occurrence of this specific shape.

ABS gateway metadata empty-error-body flap: eleventh occurrence, cycle 381, resolved by cycle 382. All eleven occurrences have now resolved within one cycle. Empty error message itself still worth fixing under code-change scope (GatewayError/next_step in monitor/checks_gateway.py).

ESTAT list_dataflows timeout pattern: twentieth episode, cycle 389 only, resolved by cycle 390, clean through cycle 391. Consistent with the usual one-cycle recovery. This episode coincided with ABS showing the identical timeout text for the first time -- see the ABS/ESTAT same-cycle item above. Watch for a twenty-first episode, and specifically whether multi-cycle persistence recurs. Standing recommendation (raise deadline, stream listing, or cache parsed result) remains open as a code-change-scope fix, not actioned by this read-only routine.

ILO gateway-data-only 403 flap (standalone): two occurrences on record, cycle 370 (resolved by 371) and cycle 322 (tail end of the cycle 321 blanket-403 episode). Both resolved within one to two cycles. No new occurrence through cycle 388 (the cycle 384 episode is a different shape: both metadata and data 403, see above). Watch for a third occurrence of this standalone data-only shape, and specifically whether it ever persists past one cycle.

SBS gateway DNS resolution flap: first occurrence, cycle 366 (`Temporary failure in name resolution` on gateway metadata, gateway data probe timed out), resolved by cycle 367. No second occurrence through cycle 388. Isolated to SBS; same failure shape previously seen for FBOS at cycle 50 (treated as infrastructure, not provider-down). Watch for a second occurrence; escalate if it recurs.

UNICEF HTTP 429 flap: sixth occurrence cycle 346, resolved by cycle 347. Prior occurrences cycle 126, 178, 262, 305, 346, all resolved within one cycle. No new occurrence through cycle 388. Watch for a seventh occurrence.

ABS and ESTAT gateway_issue coincided in the same cycle a second time, cycle 389, resolved by cycle 390. Unlike the first occurrence (cycle 319), both endpoints this time failed with byte-identical text: `gateway metadata: tool call list_dataflows timed out after 60.0s`. All ten other endpoints stayed healthy through cycle 389, ruling out the routine's own network. Strengthens, but does not confirm, a shared-cause reading (gateway/host under load) over coincidence. Watch for a third same-cycle occurrence, especially with matching failure text again.

OECD gateway_issue 403 Forbidden episode (cycles 290-292, gateway list_dataflows and gateway data probe both HTTP 403, direct path healthy throughout): resolved by cycle 293. No new occurrence through cycle 388. First occurrence of this pattern for OECD, notable for spanning three consecutive cycles (~6h). Watch for a second occurrence; escalate for real if a future episode again spans more than one cycle.

ILO direct-path 403 flap (basic checks): tenth occurrence cycle 286, resolved by cycle 287 (one cycle, as usual), clean since (superseded by the blanket 403 pattern, a different and more severe pattern -- see above). Prior occurrences cycle 32, 94, 159, 166, 202, 238, 244, 249, 267. Watch for an eleventh occurrence of this specific direct-only shape.

ILO references:contentconstraint broken (500) at cycle 274 resolved by cycle 275 (reads `ignored`, not `broken`, in the current cycle's contract rows). Second occurrence overall of this assertion flapping (first was a same-cycle blip at cycle 199). No new occurrence through cycle 388. Watch for a third occurrence; escalate if a future broken reading persists beyond one cycle.

ILO gateway_issue episode (cycles 268-269, gateway metadata HTTP 500 on list_dataflows, direct healthy throughout): resolved by cycle 270. No new occurrence through cycle 388. Distinct pattern from the cycle 322, 370, and 384 gateway data/metadata 403 episodes (see above): different HTTP status (500 vs 403). Watch separately.

ECB contract-probe 504 flap (second pattern): constraint:availableconstraint (504 -> 404) and references:none (504 -> 200) both showed a was/now change in /api/contracts between cycle 283 and 286, verdict stayed ok throughout. No further changes list entries on these assertions through cycle 388. Not the same assertions as the cycles 182-183 references:* 504 flap (that watch item is separate, still clean). Watch for recurrence on these two assertions specifically.
ABS contract 503 flap: dialect:sdmx3 and errors:missing_artefact both returned 503 at cycle 234 only, resolved by cycle 235. No new occurrence through cycle 388. Watch for a second occurrence.
ECB metadata 503 (provider_down): occurred cycle 199 only, resolved by cycle 200. No new occurrence through cycle 388. Watch for a second occurrence.
ABS gateway metadata 502 Bad Gateway flap: occurred cycle 198 only, resolved by cycle 199. No new occurrence through cycle 388. Watch for recurrence. Distinct from the empty-error-body flap above.
UNICEF direct-path HTTP 404 'no data found' flap: occurred cycle 197 only, resolved by cycle 198. No new occurrence through cycle 388. Watch for a second occurrence.
STATSNZ auth:listing capability_appeared, first seen cycle 60, still present at cycle 385: listing served without credentials. Still open, not re-reported since no new change.

Content-Type parameter order (charset vs version) on structure responses varies between requests. Cosmetic, verdict stays ok. Seen again this cycle on ABS encoding:structure_xml. Expected to keep flapping across multiple endpoints; do not re-report unless the verdict itself changes.
IMF references:* 401 flap: first and only occurrence, cycle 161, resolved by cycle 162. No new occurrence through cycle 388. Watch for a second occurrence.
ECB references:* 504 flap (cycles 182-183 pattern): first occurrence, cycles 182-183, resolved by cycle 184. No new occurrence through cycle 388. Watch for a second occurrence.
